title: Compose Companion issue close in the PWA

gates.name: companion_close_browser
gates.command: cd frontend && npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/companion-close.spec.ts

verify: Independent issue-close verification covers resolved close/duplicate, open/version/permission/archive failures, authoritative issue reread, and absence of reopen/client-derived resolution.
evidence_required: FT-016-AC-032 RED: no browser Companion issue-close consumer exists; GREEN: exact authorized close/duplicate succeeds only for current resolved issue while open/version/permission/archive cases fail without changing authoritative state and no reopen path exists; decisive comparison: strict request, response/DOM, and issue/proposal/DecisionRecord reread; artifact: close evidence under .tasks/TASK-109-T3-FT-016-W3/.
purpose: Expose resolved-issue close independently of Companion reads, invocation, and proposal decision.
success_outcome: Authorized Boss/Engineer users can close only a current resolved issue while open/stale/denied/archive paths remain non-mutating and no reopen or client-derived resolution exists.
anti_goals: Do not implement reads, invoke Companion, decide proposals, reopen issues, or derive issue resolution in the client.
Do not create Safety, Plant, Task, or provider effects from close.

stop_conditions: Close needs a command outside Companion Governance HTTP.
The UI would need to infer resolution or reopen/advance an ineligible issue.

constraints: Primary owner is Operator PWA; Companion Governance owns issue status/version and close mutation.
Submit only request_id/expected_version and render backend result.
invariants: Only a current resolved issue may close; no reopen path exists.
Denied/stale/archive close attempts produce no Task, Safety, Plant, or governance side effect.
verification_targets: FT-016-AC-032: close/duplicate plus open/version/permission/archive failures, authoritative reread, and no reopen path.
T3 harm proof uses isolated issues and confirms safe rerun/denial leaves no unauthorized governance or downstream effect.
